title: How much of an open-source chip design search can cheap fidelity rungs and proof prediction save, with a guarantee?
lede: an honest, mostly negative multi-fidelity study on real SKY130 place-and-route: cheap rungs mis-rank routed area x delay (generic-gate tau-b median -0.04), successive halving does not beat random routed search, and proof success is predicted by design size rather than by the rewrite; a theorem bounds halving's regret by the cut rungs' inversions, and a pilot with ratio below 1 certifies that halving returns a cost no worse than the pilot's best point (0 violations in 1.5 million draws), a ceiling about 2.7 times the realised regret; on a fresh 120-sequence pool the held-out schedule 'skip the generic-gate rung, keep 8' has 1.04% routed regret against 5.49% for the hand-chosen one, a gap made by one tie-heavy design. On 26 held-out designs it beats random routing of the same wall-clock where routing costs over 3 times a mapped score (2.07% against 3.59% regret) and loses where routing is cheap; a rule fixed before any routing (ladder only above a 3x cost ratio, else random) halves the regret of either policy on held-out designs (1.66% against 2.29% and 4.38%). on eight designs no table had run (milestone 113) the rule has 0.91% regret against 2.64% for random routing and 1.44% for always running the ladder. a mapped score clipped at the clock period (milestone 115) cuts that rule's regret on seven new designs, run blind, from 2.73% to 0.83%. Counted by what each rule had seen (milestone 117), the clipped switch has 1.60% regret against 2.91% for equal-cost random routing on the 24 cells of 12 designs run after its parameters were fixed (better in 18, worse in 5), while the switch without the clip is level with random routing on designs it had not seen; wide barrel shifters remain the failure. Milestones 1 to 117 are in the log
summary: An open research programme with milestones 1 to 97 logged; milestone 1 is described first, later milestones follow, and the log in the project README has the rest. Over 10 small designs, 60 ABC pass sequences each and two clock targets (1,200 runs through Yosys, ABC and OpenROAD on SKY130 HD), the generic-gate rung's Kendall tau-b against routed (global-route plus timing repair) area × period is below 0.7 on all 9 designs where it is defined (median −0.04), and its pick costs a median 13.5% of routed area × period. The liberty-mapped rung is no better than 0.59 median tau at a tight clock (median regret 10.5%) but nearly exact at a relaxed one (0% regret), because timing repair reorders designs. Routed points cost about 8× a generic point here, so there is little to save on designs this small. Limits: one corner and utilisation, global-route estimates, ten small designs. Milestone 2 replays search on the cached table at equal wall-clock: screening the pool at the generic-gate or mapped rung and verifying the top points does not beat random or hill-climbing search (45 s: regret 1.08% and 1.27% against 0.94% and 0.61%), and loses badly at smaller budgets. Hypotheses H2 to H5 (multi-fidelity wins, coverage, proof prediction) are not yet run. Milestone 3 replays successive halving across the four rungs: starting from the generic-gate rung it is the worst strategy (about 10% mean routed regret at the tight clock at 45 s against 0.94% for random search); starting at the mapped rung wins on most designs at a relaxed clock but loses heavily on two; a 6-point routed pilot that picks the start rung recovers the designs plain halving loses (H3), so there is no multi-fidelity gain at equal wall-clock on this 50-point pool yet. Milestone 4 (H4) replays conformal shortlists: a routed pilot of 10 to 16 points calibrates a one-sided bound on routed area × delay from a cheap rung. On the mapped rung the routed optimum is kept 0.99 of the time at nominal 0.90 (0.90–0.92 at 0.80) while routing 42–57% of the pool, against 0.53–0.65 for random search with equal routed runs; on the generic-gate rung coverage is 0.65 at nominal 0.80, no better than random search, so H4 is refuted there. Limits: 20 groups from 10 small designs, one corner. H5 (milestone 5): across 752 Yosys SAT-miter proofs of ABC rewrites on 15 designs, proof time is set by design size (multiplier median 0.01 s at 4 bits, 11 s at 8, over 10 s at 9–10) and never by a rewrite failing; leave-one-design-out AUC is high pooled (0.96–0.998) only because it reads design size, and within the 8-bit multiplier it is 0.65–0.78 against 0.81 for the rule “the rewrite shrinks the netlist”. One solver, one timeout. Milestone 6 (theory): define a rung’s inversion as the largest log-factor by which it ranks a truly worse candidate at or ahead of a better one; halving’s routed regret is then at most the sum of the cut rungs’ inversions (proved; holds on all 40 table cells). It is vacuous for the generic-gate rung (inversion above 0.3 on 8 of 10 groups) and loose for the mapped rungs (bound 0.23–0.35 against about 0 realised); a 10-point pilot sees a median 52–67% of the inversion but cannot certify it. The probabilistic version is open.
